note_sections.t: Re-evaluation for management of biopsy-proven prostate adenocarcinoma following recent PSA progression and MRI confirmation.

Long-standing referral for prostate cancer management. The patient is a 62-year-old retired baker, married but currently living alone, with his adult daughter serving as the primary contact. He reports a sedentary lifestyle with only occasional walking and consumes no alcohol. His medical history is significant for type 2 diabetes managed with metformin and empagliflozin, COPD treated with tiotropium and salbutamol PRN, obesity, and osteoarthritis. He has mild lower urinary tract symptoms with an IPSS score of 3/35. Recent appointments include a vascular surgery consultation for varicose veins. He prefers phone follow-up due to living over 90 minutes from the clinic.

On DRE, the prostate is smooth, symmetric, and non-tender, consistent with clinical stage cT1c. General examination reveals a stable patient with normal cardiopulmonary findings and no signs of metastatic disease. Vital signs are within normal limits, with blood pressure 125/73 mmHg and heart rate 69 bpm.
